answer.answer: The study cannot answer the question. The validity gate kept no runs, so there is no evidence about which combinations of plan bias and hand-off speed make the ego leave its lane, and none of the 5 challenging cases was confirmed, as the goal status says. Every run was rejected. The first runs (+0.5 m at 1.4x on the first five scenes) stopped with HALT, and every later run was rejected with no reason recorded. That includes the unperturbed baseline runs (0 m, 1.0x), which these scenes passed when they were chosen, so the cause is probably the run setup, not the policy. Also, every rejected run lists its controller as "linear", not VaVAM. So even if these runs had been kept, they would not have tested the policy the question asks about.
open: Why the gate rejected every run: the early +0.5 m / 1.4x runs halted, and the rest, including the 0 m / 1.0x baselines on several scenes, were rejected without a recorded reason. This needs fixing before any rerun, because baselines failing the gate point to a setup or pipeline fault rather than to the bias and speed settings.
The controller recorded for every run is "linear", not VaVAM. Confirm that the study is configured to run VaVAM, or the results will not answer the question.

Once 0 m / 1.0x baseline runs pass the gate on each scene, rerun the corner search at ±0.3 to ±0.5 m bias and 1.2x to 1.4x speed across the 12 scenes. Then repeat any setting that fails until its 90% range clears 0.5, so the 5 hardest cases (one per scene) can be confirmed.
Whether any setting causes a side or front collision or leaving the road, and the ranking of near misses by closest approach, are both still unknown.
